name: Duonychus
sum: Two-fingered therizinosaurid from the Late Cretaceous Bayanshiree Formation of Mongolia.
holotype: Partial skeleton with vertebrae, most of the forelimbs and part of the pelvis, Bayanshiree Formation, eastern Gobi, Mongolia.
material: Only the holotype, excavated in 2012 during the construction of a pipeline.
exceptional: A preserved keratinous claw sheath (Kobayashi et al. 2025).
biology: Described as a didactyl (two-fingered) therizinosaur, with a keratinous claw sheath preserved on one finger.
author: Kobayashi et al. 2025

sources.text: Y. Kobayashi, D. K. Zelenitsky, and A. R. Fiorillo, T. Chinzorig. 2025. Didactyl therizinosaur with a preserved keratinous claw from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia. iScience
